title: What If All Plastic Waste Got Recycled?

scenes.text: What if every piece of plastic waste got recycled? Today, almost none of it does.
In 2019 the world produced 353 million tons of plastic waste, more than double the amount in 2000.
Only 9 percent was recycled. About 15 percent was collected for recycling, but 40 percent of that was rejected as residue.
Another 19 percent was burned, and 50 percent went to landfill.
The last 22 percent was mismanaged: dumped, burned in the open, or left to leak into rivers and seas.
So recycling it all would mean recycling eleven times more than we do now. Nine percent is the number to beat.

description:
What if all plastic waste got recycled?
According to the OECD, only 9 percent of the 353 million tons of plastic waste in 2019 was recycled; 19 percent was burned, 50 percent landfilled and 22 percent mismanaged.
